q: If Person B determines that there is a significant reason making it difficult to continue the marriage due to Person A's gambling addiction, can Person B file for judicial divorce? Additionally, when does this right to file expire?
a: According to Article 840 of the Civil Code, Person B may file for divorce if there is a significant reason making it difficult to continue the marriage with Person A. Pursuant to Article 842 of the Civil Code, Person B's right to file for divorce expires 6 months from the day they became aware of Person A's gambling addiction, or 2 years from the occurrence of the reason. Therefore, Person B must file for divorce within 6 months from the day they became aware of the gambling addiction.

If one spouse has been extremely maltreated by the other spouse or his/her lineal ascendants;4. If one spouse's lineal ascendant has been extremely maltreated by the other spouse;5. q: If an employee, Person A, who is undergoing treatment for an occupational injury, suffers an additional injury due to medical malpractice while receiving treatment at an industrial accident insurance medical institution, can this incident be recognized as an occupational injury?
a: If Person A, while undergoing treatment for an occupational injury, sustains an additional injury due to medical malpractice during treatment at an industrial accident insurance medical institution, this incident is recognized as an occupational accident under Article 32, Item 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act. Specifically, if the medical malpractice occurred during the treatment process and is closely related to the original occupational injury, and it arose as part of the treatment, it can be recognized as a continued occupational injury.

path.text: If an employee suffers any injury, disease, or disability or dies due to any of the following causes, it shall be deemed an occupational accident: Provided, That this shall not apply where there is no proximate causal relation between his or her duties and the accident: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2010; Oct. 24, 2017; Jan. 15, 2019>1. Accident on duty:(a) Any accident that occurs while he or she performs a duty under his or her employment contract or other acts incidental thereto;(b) Any accident that occurs while he or she uses a facility, etc. provided by his or her business owner, due to any defect in or any careless management of such facility, etc.;(c) Deleted; <Oct. 24, 2017>(d) Any accident that occurs while he or she participates in an event sponsored by or under the direction of his or her business owner or prepares for such event;(e) Any accident that occurs at recess due to an act deemed to be under the control and management of his or her business owner;(f) Any other accident that occurs in connection with his or her duties;2. Occupational disease:(a) Any disease caused by handling or being exposed to any physical agent, chemical substance, dust, pathogen, work imposing a burden on his or her body, or any other agent causing trouble to his or her health while performing his or her duties;(b) Any disease caused by an occupational injury;(c) Any disease caused by work-related mental stress due to workplace harassment, verbal abuse from customers, etc. under Article 76-2 of the Labor Standards Act;(d) Any other disease caused in connection with his or her duties;3. Accident on commuting:(a) Any accident that occurs while he or she commutes to or from work using a transportation means provided by his or her business owner or another similar means under the control and management of his or her business owner;(b) Any accident that occurs while he or she commutes to or from work using other common route and method.

path.text: Article 5 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Jan. 27, 2010; May 20, 2010; Jun. 4, 2010; Dec. 18, 2012; Oct. 24, 2017; Jun. 12, 2018; May 26, 2020>1. The term "occupational accident" means any injury, disease, disability or death of an employee which is caused by an occupational reason;2. The terms "employee", "wage", "average wage", and "ordinary wage" mean such "employee", "wage", "average wage", and "ordinary wage", respectively as defined in the Labor Standards Act: Provided, That where it is deemed difficult to determine a "wage" or "average wage" pursuant to the Labor Standards Act, the amount determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Employment and Labor shall be the relevant "wage" or "average wage";3. The term "survivor" means a spouse (including a person who is in a de facto marital relationship; the same shall apply hereinafter), children, parent, grandchild, grandparent, brother, or sister of the deceased person;4. The term "cure" means reaching a state in which an injury or disease has been completely cured or there are no further expected effects of treatment with its symptoms remaining unchanged;5. The term "disability" means a state in which an injury or disease has been cured, but the ability to work has been lost or diminished due to mental or physical damage;6. The term "invalidity" means a state in which the ability to work has been lost or diminished due to mental or physical damage caused by an occupational injury or disease, which remains uncured;7. The term "pneumoconiosis" means a lung disease, the main symptom of which is fibroplastic proliferation caused by the inhalation of dust particles;8. The term "commuting" means a movement between a residence and a place of employment or from one place of employment to another place of employment in relation with employment.

q: If Person A conducts an event similar to the sports promotion voting rights system, offering prizes or financial benefits to those who correctly predict outcomes, and Person B participates in this event for gambling purposes, what penalties do Person A and Person B face, respectively?
a: Person A, by engaging in activities similar to those regulated under the National Sports Promotion Act, violates Article 26, Paragraph 1 of the Act. Consequently, under Article 47 of the National Sports Promotion Act, Person A may be subject to imprisonment for up to 7 years or a fine not exceeding 70 million won. Person B, having used this similar activity for gambling, falls under the provisions of Article 48, Item 3 of the National Sports Promotion Act, and may face imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine not exceeding 50 million won.

q: How many times can Person A and Person B conduct broadcast speeches and newspaper advertisements during the presidential election campaign period?
a: Person A and Person B may each conduct broadcast speeches up to 11 times on both television and radio. Regarding newspaper advertisements, Person A (or the political party to which Person A belongs, if Person A is a party-nominated candidate) may place advertisements up to 70 times. However, when calculating the number of advertisements in daily newspapers, placing an advertisement in one daily newspaper is counted as one instance.

An election of proportional representation members of the National Assembly:One time by television and radio broadcast, respectively, and each time within 10 minutes by two representatives appointed by a political party from among candidates for proportional representation members of the National Assembly, respectively;3. Election of the National Assembly members of local constituencies and the heads of autonomous Gus/Sis/Guns:Up to two times by television and radio broadcast, respectively, and each time within 10 minutes by a candidate using local broadcasting facilities;4. Election of the proportional representative City/Do council members:One time within 10 minutes by television and radio broadcast, respectively, using local broadcasting facilities by a representative elected by each party from among the candidates for the relevant election at each constituency of proportional representative City/Do council members;5. An election of Mayors/Do Governors:Up to five times by television and radio broadcast, respectively, using local broadcasting facilities, each time within 10 minutes by candidate.

q: Person A wishes to purchase Person B's land. In this case, how should the anticipated purchase price be determined, and under what criteria can Person B's land be deemed eligible for purchase?
a:
The anticipated purchase price should be determined based on the standard market value as prescribed by Article 4 of the Local Tax Act at the time of the purchase request. If there is no standard market value available, the price should be assessed by comparing transaction cases of similar properties within the vicinity.

For Person B's land to be deemed eligible for purchase, it must meet the criteria where the land's utility has diminished due to the inability to use it for its original purpose, or where use and enjoyment are impossible due to legal restrictions. Additionally, there must be no fault attributable to Person B regarding the reduction in utility or the impossibility of use and enjoyment of the land.

q: When issuing an air pollution alert, which pollutants does Person B City target, and how are the alert levels categorized based on their concentration?
a: Person B City designates particulate matter (PM-10), fine particulate matter (PM-2.5), and ozone (O3) as the target pollutants for air pollution alerts. The alert levels are categorized based on the concentration of these pollutants as follows: for particulate matter (PM-10) and fine particulate matter (PM-2.5), the levels are divided into advisory and alert stages; for ozone (O3), the levels are divided into advisory, alert, and severe alert stages.

q: When can Person A and Person B commence their respective election campaigns, and what is the amount of the deposit required upon candidate registration for each?
a: Election campaigns may only be conducted from the commencement of the election period until the day before the election. If Person A is running for the presidential election, a deposit of 300 million Korean Won must be paid upon candidate registration. If Person B is running for a constituency in the parliamentary election, a deposit of 15 million Korean Won must be paid upon candidate registration. However, if Person A or Person B is registered as a person with a disability under Article 32 of the "Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities," or is 29 years of age or younger on the election day, they are required to pay 50% of the aforementioned amounts. If they are between 30 and 39 years of age, they are required to pay 70% of the aforementioned amounts.

path.text: Article 59 (Period for Election Campaign) An election campaign may be allowed during the period from the commencing date of election period to the day before the election day: Provided, That the same shall not apply to any of the following cases: <Amended on Mar. 12, 2004; Aug. 4, 2005; Jul. 28, 2011; Feb. 29, 2012; Feb. 8, 2017; Dec. 29, 2020>1. Where any preliminary candidate, etc. wages the election campaign pursuant to Article 60-3 (1) and (2);2. Where a person works on an election campaign by sending text messages. In such cases, the persons who are permitted to send such messages by means of automatic broadcast communications (referring to means by which text messages are sent by automatically selecting recipients using a program even where the number of persons intended to receive messages at the same time exceeds 20 or the number of such persons is not more than 20; hereinafter the same shall apply) shall be limited to candidates and preliminary candidates, but the number of times such messages may be sent shall not exceed eight times (including the number of times a candidate sent such messages when he or she was a preliminary candidate), and only one telephone number reported in accordance with the National Election Commission Regulations shall be used;3. Where a person works on an election campaign by posting a writing or video clip on an internet web-site or its bulletin board or chatting room or sending an e-mail (referring to a communication system with which computer users exchange information in the form of text, voice, images, or video clips through a network; hereinafter the same shall apply). In such cases, persons who are permitted to send e-mails by entrusting the dispatch of e-mails to an agency shall be limited to candidates and preliminary candidates.4. Where an election campaign is conducted by telephone (limited to direct telephone conversations between a caller and a receiver, excluding telephones equipped with automatic transmission devices using computers) or by words (excluding cases using a loudspeaker system or targeting the general public at an outdoor assembly) when it is not an election day;5. Where a person who intends to become a candidate gives his or her name card by means referred to in Article 60-3 (1) 2 (including the proviso of that subparagraph) during the period from 180 days before the election day (in cases of a presidential election, referring to 240 days before the election day) to the date of application for the registration of preliminary candidate for the relevant election.[Title Amended on Jul. 28, 2011]

q: What procedures must Person A follow when imposing disciplinary action on Person B, and what are the possible disciplinary measures for Person B's violent behavior?
a: When Person A imposes disciplinary action on Person B, a resolution must first be obtained from a disciplinary committee composed of at least three crew members. For Person B's violent behavior, possible disciplinary measures include admonishment, prohibition from disembarking, and dismissal from the ship. However, dismissal from the ship should only be imposed if it is evident that Person B's actions, such as violent behavior, have disrupted order on the ship or have intentionally caused significant interference with the ship's operation.

q: In the case where Person A and Person B reported false financial information to a public official, resulting in the inclusion of inaccurate facts in the original notarial deed, and used this as the basis for applying for company incorporation registration, how should the registrar handle this application, and what criminal penalties could Person A and Person B face?
a: The act of Person A and Person B causing inaccurate facts to be recorded in the original notarial deed through false reporting is punishable under Article 228, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Act, with imprisonment for up to five years or a fine of up to 10 million won. Using this in a registration application is punishable under Article 229 of the Criminal Act with the penalty prescribed for the offense. Furthermore, applying for company incorporation registration based on such a falsely created notarial deed falls under the category of "cases where there is a cause for nullity or cancellation of the matters to be registered" according to Article 26, Item 10 of the Commercial Registration Act. Therefore, the registrar must reject the application, providing reasons for the rejection.

path.text: Any person who makes a false report to a public official and has that official enter record any false fact in the authentic deed or identical special media records, such as electronic records, shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than five years or a fine not exceeding ten million won. <Amended on Dec. 29, 1995>

Where an application for any other registration required to be filed simultaneously has not been filed simultaneously;13. Where the case violates Article 38 (3), 39 (2), or the proviso to Article 40 (1);17. Where a registration licence tax for registration or a fee under Article 22 (3) is unpaid, or any other obligation imposed by other Acts in relation to an application for registration has not been peformed.

q: When Person A's friend, Person C, wishes to make a repayment on behalf of Person A, is it legally permissible to do so before the due date, and if Person B refuses, what legal methods are available to offer the repayment?
a: Under Article 469, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Act, Person C, as a third party, can repay the debt to Person B on behalf of Person A, provided there is no explicit agreement between the parties prohibiting third-party repayment. Additionally, according to Article 468 of the Civil Act, repayment can be made before the due date unless there are specific restrictions, but if this causes any damage to Person B, compensation for the damage must be provided. If Person B refuses Person C's repayment, under Article 460 of the Civil Act, Person C can offer the repayment by notifying Person B that the repayment is ready and demanding acceptance.

q: On what grounds can Person A file for a retrial concerning the conviction?
a: Person A can file for a retrial of the conviction based on the final determination of the invalidity of Person B's copyright. According to Article 420, Item 6 of the Criminal Procedure Act, a retrial can be requested if a conviction for copyright infringement is based on a right that has been subsequently declared invalid.

path.text: Article 420 (Reasons for Reopening of Procedures) A request for reopening of procedure may be made for the benefit of a person against whom a judgment of "guilty" has become final and conclusive, where any of the following causes exists:1. When documentary evidence or articles of evidence, on which the original judgment was based, have been proved by another finally binding judgment to have been forged or altered;2. When testimony, expert opinion, interpretation, or translation on which the original judgment was based, has been proved by another finally binding judgment to be false;3. When the offense of false accusation committed against a person pronounced guilty has been proved by another final judgment;4. When the decision on which the original judgment was based has been altered by another final decision;5. When clear evidence has been newly discovered that in regard to a person pronounced guilty, a judgment of "not guilty" or acquittal of a prosecution should be pronounced, or in the case of a person condemned, a judgment of remission of punishment should be pronounced, or a lighter offense than that found by the original judgment should be given;6. When, in a case in which a judgment of "guilty" has been rendered for the offense of infringing a copyright, a patent right, a utility model right, a design right, or a trademark right, a final decision of the Korea Industrial Property Office holding such right to be void has been made or a judgment of a court has been rendered to the same effect;7. When it is proved by a final judgment that an offense had been committed in connection with official functions by a judge who participated in the original judgment or the judgment of the preceding trial, or in the inquiry which formed the basis of such judgment, or by a prosecutor or senior judicial police officer who participated in the institution of a public prosecution or in the investigation which formed the basis of the public prosecution: Provided, That where public prosecution was instituted against such judge, prosecutor, or senior judicial police officer prior to the rendition of the original judgment, this shall apply only when the court which rendered the original judgment was unaware of such facts.[This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 8, 2020]

q: Person B purchased land from Person A and has paid the full purchase price, but the registration has not yet been completed. Can it be considered that Person B has acquired ownership of the land?
a: The acquisition or loss of real property rights resulting from legal acts such as the sale of real estate becomes effective only upon registration. Since Person B has not completed the registration for the land they purchased, it cannot be considered that Person B has acquired ownership of the land.

q: If the construction prohibition clause in the land sale contract between Person A and Person B is void, does this render the entire contract void?
a: The general principle is that if a part of a contract is void, the entire contract becomes void. However, if it can be acknowledged that the parties would have entered into the contract even without the void provision, the remaining parts of the contract do not become void. Therefore, if it is recognized that Person A and Person B would have entered into the sale contract even without the construction provision, the rest of the contract remains valid.

q: When Person A, as the chairman of the board of an educational foundation, intends to sell a plot of land that constitutes basic property, and the sale is not a minor matter as defined by Presidential Decree, is it subject to approval by the competent authority? Furthermore, is this a matter that must be deliberated and resolved by the board of directors? Additionally, if the sale of the basic property plot could potentially bring significant benefits to Person A's family, is Person A allowed to participate in the decision-making process regarding this matter?

The disposition of basic property is subject to deliberation and resolution by the board of directors. q: In the event that an accident occurs due to Person B's negligence, and Person A's insurance company compensates Person C for part of the resulting damages, what rights does Person A's insurance company acquire, and what claims can Person C make against the insurance company?
a: When Person A's insurance company compensates Person C for part of the damages resulting from an accident caused by Person B's negligence, the insurance company acquires the right of subrogation to Person C's claim for damages against Person B or Person A, up to the amount paid, pursuant to Article 682(1) of the Commercial Act. Additionally, under Article 724(2) of the Commercial Act, Person C can directly claim compensation from the insurance company for their damages within the limits of the insurance coverage. Furthermore, according to Article 719 of the Commercial Act, Person C can demand that the insurance company assume the liability for compensation that Person B owes to Person C.

path.text: If a loss has occurred due to acts committed by a third party, the insurer that has paid the amount of insurance coverage shall acquire the rights the policyholder or the insured has against the third party to the extent of the amount of insurance coverage paid: Provided, That where the insurer has paid part of the amount of insurance coverage payable, it may exercise such rights to the extent it does not injure the rights the insured has.

q: What are the necessary conditions for Person A to obtain confirmation of compliance for their waste management business, and what is the application procedure to obtain it?
a: According to Article 25-3, Paragraph 1 of the Waste Management Act, the following conditions must be met: 1. The business must comply with the standards and methods for waste treatment as prescribed in Article 13 of the Waste Management Act, or adhere to the principles and compliance requirements for waste recycling as outlined in Article 13-2, as determined by the Ordinance of the Ministry of Environment. 2. The business must not fall under any disqualifications as specified in Article 26. 3. All legal responsibilities arising from violations of this Act must have been fulfilled. Additionally, pursuant to Paragraph 2 of the same Article, Person A must apply to the Minister of Environment or the Mayor/Provincial Governor, attaching the necessary documentation to confirm compliance with the aforementioned conditions, at least three months before the expiration of the validity period for the confirmation of compliance for their business type. Unless there are special circumstances, Person A will be notified of the compliance status before the expiration date.

q: What procedures must Person B follow to verify Person A's resident registration certificate, and how should the situation be handled if Person A fails to submit the interim prepayment estimation report?
a: Person B must verify Person A's resident registration certificate as of the end of the tax period through the shared use of administrative information pursuant to Article 36, Paragraph 1 of the "Electronic Government Act." However, if Person A does not consent to this verification or if the resident registration certificate cannot be used to determine the presence of dependents, Person A should be required to attach either the resident registration certificate or a certificate of family relations registration. Additionally, if Person A fails to submit the interim prepayment estimation report, Person B may investigate and determine Person A's comprehensive income amount by applying the provisions of Article 80 of the Income Tax Act.

q: Does Person B automatically acquire beneficiary rights upon being designated as a beneficiary under the trust instrument? Furthermore, what are the legal effects if Person B renounces the beneficiary rights? Additionally, upon Person C's appointment as the successor trustee, under what criteria does Person C assume the obligations related to the existing administration of the trust?
a: Under Article 56, Paragraph 1 of the Trust Act, Person B, designated as a beneficiary by the trust instrument, automatically acquires beneficiary rights unless otherwise specified in the trust instrument. If Person B expresses an intention to renounce the beneficiary rights, according to Article 57, Paragraph 2 of the Trust Act, it is deemed as if Person B never had the beneficiary rights from the outset, unless such renunciation infringes upon the rights of a third party, in which case the effect is limited. Meanwhile, when Person C is appointed as the successor trustee in place of the original trustee, under Article 53, Paragraph 2 of the Trust Act, any claims arising from the administration of the trust by the original trustee can be asserted against Person C, but only to the extent of the trust property.

q: What are the formal requirements that must be included in a judgment document in a civil lawsuit, and what legal effect arises if the 'reasons' are omitted or contradictory? Through what procedure can Person B respond in such a case?
a: According to Article 208, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Act, a judgment document must include the parties and their legal representatives, the order, the purport of the claim and the purport of the appeal, the reasons, the date the arguments were concluded (or the date of pronouncement), and the court, and it must be signed and sealed by the judge who rendered the judgment. Pursuant to Article 208, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Act, the reasons section of the judgment must indicate the court's assessment of the parties' claims and methods of attack and defense to the extent that the order can be deemed justified. If the judgment document fails to state the reasons or if there are contradictions in the reasons, this constitutes an absolute ground for appeal under Article 424, Paragraph 1, Item 6 of the Civil Procedure Act, thereby granting Person B a legitimate reason to file an appeal. Consequently, Person B can respond by appealing the judgment.

q: In the event that Person B wishes to file a claim against Person D for the return of the statutory reserved portion, what is the statute of limitations for such a claim, and can the gift made by Person A during his lifetime be included in the calculation of the statutory reserved portion? Additionally, how is the statutory reserved portion calculated?
a: According to Article 1117 of the Civil Code, Person B must file a claim for the return of the statutory reserved portion within one year from the later of the date of the commencement of the inheritance (March 1, 2022) or the date when Person B became aware of the gift (April 1, 2022). Therefore, the claim must be filed by April 1, 2023, or it will be barred by the statute of limitations. Furthermore, the gift of 100 million won made by Person A to Person D falls within one year prior to the commencement of the inheritance (May 2021) and is thus included in the calculation of the statutory reserved portion pursuant to Article 1114 of the Civil Code. The amount of the statutory reserved portion is calculated by adding the value of Person A's estate at the time of the commencement of the inheritance to the amount of the gift, and then subtracting the total amount of Person A's debts, as stipulated in Article 1113, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Code.

path.text: Article 1117 (Extinctive Prescription) The right to demand the return in this Chapter shall be extinguished by prescription, if it is not exercised within one year from the time when the person entitled to a legal reserve of inheritance becomes aware of the fact that the inheritance has commenced and that gifts or testamentary gifts, which are to be returned, were made. The above right shall also be extinguished by prescription if ten years have elapsed from the time of the commencement of the inheritance.[This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 31, 1977]

Furthermore, by demonstrating that Person A's trademark is used for a distinct purpose that is identifiable and separate from Person B's goods, it may be determined, according to the definition of a trademark, that the 'trademark' or 'mark' is not intended to identify another's goods.

path.text: The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Feb. 3, 2022>1. The term "trademark" means a mark used to distinguish goods (including services or goods related to the provision of services except goods on which a geographical indication is used; hereinafter the same shall apply) of one business from those of others;2. The term "mark" means all indications used to identify the source of goods, irrespective of the composition or methods of the expression thereof, which include any sign, letter, figure, sound, smell, three-dimensional shape, hologram, movement, color, etc.;3. The term "collective mark" means a mark intended to be used directly by a corporation jointly incorporated by persons who produce, manufacture, process or sell goods, or who provide services, or intended to be used by its members;4. The term "geographical indication" means an indication used to identify goods produced, manufactured, or processed in a specific area in cases where a certain quality, reputation or other characteristic of goods has essentially originated from such specific area;5. The term "homonymous geographical indication" means a geographical indication for the same goods which shares the same pronunciation with a geographical indication of other goods, but the relevant geographical location is different from that other indication;6. The term "collective mark with geographical indication" means a mark intended to be used directly by a corporation jointly incorporated by persons who produce, manufacture, or process goods on which a geographical indication may be used, or is intended to be used by its members;7. The term "certification mark" means a mark used by a person who commercially certifies and manages the quality, place of origin, methods of production, or other characteristics of goods to certify that goods of others meet quality criteria, the place of origin, methods of production, or other characteristics;8. The term "certification mark with geographical indication" means a mark used by a person who commercially certifies a geographical indication to certify that goods of others meet specified geographical characteristics;9. The term "business emblem" means a mark used by a person who engages in not-for-profit business to identify his or her business;10. The term "registered trademark" means a trademark which has been registered;11. The term "use of a trademark" means any of the following:(a) Displaying a trademark on goods or packages of goods;(b) Transferring or delivering goods or packages of goods on which a trademark is displayed, providing such goods or packages through telecommunications lines, or exhibiting, exporting, or importing them for the purpose of such transfer, delivery, or provision;(c) Displaying a trademark on advertisements for goods, price tags, transaction documents, or other means, and exhibiting or giving wide publicity to the trademark.

q: What are the required procedures for the police to summon, arrest, or detain Person A, and what information must be communicated to him upon arrest? Furthermore, what procedures must be followed to seize or search Person A's residence?

q: Under what conditions is the capital gain from the sale of bonds or securities under a repurchase agreement distinguished, and can the income from bonds sold under a repurchase condition be considered interest income? Furthermore, when a financial company operates products that combine derivatives with interest-generating bonds, what are the conditions under which such income is taxed as interest income?
a: The capital gain from a repurchase agreement refers to the gain from the sale of bonds or securities under a repurchase or resale condition, applying a pre-agreed interest rate according to the repurchase period, as defined in Article 24 of the Enforcement Decree of the Income Tax Act. When bonds, etc., are sold under a repurchase condition, the seller is deemed to have interest income for the amount equivalent to the interest generated from the bonds, etc., out of the amount received from the buyer until the repurchase date, pursuant to Article 26, Paragraph 6 of the Enforcement Decree of the Income Tax Act. Additionally, in the case of complex financial products operated by a financial company, where interest-bearing products and derivatives are combined and effectively operated as a single product, the interest income generated from such products is taxed as interest income under Paragraph 5 of the same Article, provided certain conditions are met. These conditions include structural integration or guaranteed returns.

q: If Person B does not file an objection to the mediation decision, what legal effect does the mediation decision have? Furthermore, if there was a defect in Person C's litigation capacity, but it was rectified and Person B ratified the decision, does the ratification have retroactive effect?
a: If Person B does not file an objection to the mediation decision within the prescribed period, pursuant to Article 34, Paragraph 4, Item 1 of the Civil Mediation Act, the mediation decision has the same effect as a judicial settlement. Additionally, even if there was a defect in Person C's litigation capacity, if this defect is subsequently rectified and Person B ratifies the action, according to Articles 60 and 97 of the Civil Procedure Act, the legal action becomes retroactively valid. Therefore, if Person B accepts and ratifies the mediation decision without objection, despite the temporary defect in the legal representative's capacity, the mediation decision is validly confirmed and its effect is retroactive.

a: When Person A receives treatment at an external medical facility, the warden must promptly inform Person A's family of this fact. In cases where the treatment is necessitated by Person A's intentional actions or gross negligence, as in this scenario, Person A may be required to bear all or part of the medical expenses.

q: In the event that Person A conceals illegal assets, making forfeiture impossible, what measures can the court take regarding the disposition of such assets? Additionally, is it possible to execute against Person B's inherited assets after Person A's death, and what is the statute of limitations for such forfeiture and confiscation?
a: If Person A acquired illegal assets through a public official crime but the assets are concealed, making forfeiture impossible, the court may impose a monetary equivalent of the assets pursuant to Article 6 of the Special Act on Forfeiture for Public Official Crimes. The statute of limitations for forfeiture and confiscation is 10 years, as stipulated in Article 9-4 of the same Act. Furthermore, even after Person A's death, execution against Person B's inherited assets is permissible under Article 478 of the Criminal Procedure Act.

q: Under what conditions can Person B rescind the contract if Person A fails to fulfill their contractual obligations, and how does the presence of other clauses in the contract affect this?
a: Person B may rescind the contract by setting a reasonable period for performance and, if performance is not rendered within that period, may proceed with rescission. q: If Person A attempts to purchase a life insurance policy with his 14-year-old son, Person B, as the insured, where Person B's death is the insured event, is such a contract valid? Additionally, how do the regulations concerning life and accident insurance apply when purchasing health insurance, and can the insurer propose contract terms that are disadvantageous to Person A as a special agreement?
a: If Person A attempts to purchase a life insurance policy with his 14-year-old son, Person B, as the insured, where Person B's death is the insured event, such an insurance contract is void. However, it is possible to enter into a health insurance contract with Person B as the insured, and in this case, the provisions concerning life and accident insurance may be applied mutatis mutandis to the extent that they do not contradict the nature of the health insurance. Furthermore, when entering into a health insurance contract, the insurer cannot alter the contract terms to the disadvantage of the policyholder, Person A, or the insured, Person B.

q: In the event that Person A faces a clear risk of disadvantageous actions while preparing a public interest report, what application can they make, and what legal protection can they request if they have already suffered disadvantageous actions? Additionally, what procedures must the Commission follow upon receiving such a protection request?
a: If Person A faces a clear risk of disadvantageous actions during the preparation of a public interest report, they may apply to the Commission for a prohibition of disadvantageous actions under Article 22, Paragraph 1 of the Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Act. Furthermore, if Person A has already suffered disadvantageous actions, they may request necessary protective measures, such as restoration to the original state, from the Commission under Article 17, Paragraph 1 of the same Act. In this regard, the Commission is required to make a decision and recommendation on the protective measures within 60 days from the date of receiving the protection request, in accordance with Article 16, Paragraph 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Act. If necessary, the period may be extended within a range of up to 30 days.

q: In the event that Person A suffers an accident due to Person C's driving error, what rights does Person B Insurance Company acquire, and what rights can Person D exercise against Person B Insurance Company regarding their injuries?

q: In a situation where there is no separate evidence to prove the criminal conduct of Person A, apart from the evidence collected through unlawful procedures, on what legal basis should the court render a not guilty verdict, and what is the procedure for determining the publication of the not guilty verdict?
a: Evidence collected by investigative authorities without following lawful procedures cannot be used as evidence pursuant to Article 308-2 of the Criminal Procedure Act. Therefore, if the remaining evidence is insufficient to prove the criminal conduct, the court must render a not guilty verdict in accordance with Article 325 of the Criminal Procedure Act. Upon rendering a not guilty verdict, the court must declare the intent to publish the verdict as per Article 58(2) of the Criminal Act. However, if the defendant, Person A, does not consent to the publication or if consent cannot be obtained, the publication may be exceptionally omitted.

q: When serving litigation documents to Person A, who lacks the capacity to litigate, and one of the joint legal representatives, Person B, is stationed at a military facility, through whom and how should the service be effected?
a: According to Article 179 of the Civil Procedure Act, documents to be served to a person lacking the capacity to litigate must be served to their legal representative. If there are multiple legal representatives, Article 180 of the Civil Procedure Act stipulates that service to just one of them is sufficient. Furthermore, if the person to be served is stationed at a military facility, Article 181 of the Civil Procedure Act requires that service be made to the head of that facility. Therefore, in this case, the documents should be served to Person C, or if serving Person B, it must be done through the head of the military facility where Person B is stationed.

q: Under what circumstances can a court sever or consolidate trials for crimes jointly committed by Person A and Person B, and in the event that Person B appeals, under what conditions can the original judgment against Person A also be overturned?
a: The crime jointly committed by Person A and Person B constitutes a related case under Article 11, Item 2 of the Criminal Procedure Act. Pursuant to Article 300 of the Criminal Procedure Act, the court may, if deemed necessary, decide to sever or consolidate the trials either ex officio or upon the application of the prosecutor, defendant, or defense counsel. Furthermore, if the reason for overturning the original judgment in Person B's appeal equally applies to Person A, the court must also overturn the original judgment against Person A in accordance with Article 364-2 of the Criminal Procedure Act. Therefore, even if only Person B appeals, if the grounds for overturning the judgment are common to both, the original judgment against Person A must also be overturned.

q: How should Person A delegate the ticket sales to Person B, and what are the licensing standards for Person A's terminal expansion plan?
a: Person A should delegate the ticket sales to Person B through the terminal operator. However, if it is deemed necessary for the convenience of passengers, Person B may sell tickets directly or delegate ticket sales to an entity other than the terminal operator. Additionally, the licensing standards for Person A's terminal expansion plan require that the terminal's location be convenient for passenger use and easily connected to other modes of transportation. q: What are the requirements for Person A, as the creditor, to interrupt the statute of limitations through the provisional attachment of Person B's property, and how is the statute of limitations calculated if it is interrupted by the attachment?
a: Provisional attachment is one of the grounds for interrupting the statute of limitations under Article 168 of the Civil Code. However, if the person benefiting from the statute of limitations, Person B, is not notified of the attachment, the interruption of the statute of limitations does not take effect. Therefore, the interruption of the statute of limitations is recognized only after Person B is notified of the provisional attachment. Once the statute of limitations is interrupted, the period that elapsed prior to the interruption is not included in the calculation of the statute of limitations, and a new statute of limitations period begins to run from the point when the reason for the interruption ceases.

q: If Person B establishes a severance pay system, what criteria should be used to set it, and how are the average wage and retirement pension systems defined?
a: When Person B establishes a severance pay system, it must be set up to provide a severance payment of at least 30 days' worth of the average wage for each year of continuous service. The average wage is defined as the total amount of wages paid to the employee during the three months preceding the date on which the reason for calculation arises, divided by the total number of days in that period. Additionally, the retirement pension system includes the defined benefit retirement pension plan, the defined contribution retirement pension plan, and the individual retirement pension plan.

path.text: The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Mar. 20, 2018; Jan. 15, 2019; May 26, 2020>1. The term "employee" means a person, regardless of the kind of occupation, who offers labor to business or a workplace for the purpose of earning wages;2. The term "employer" means a business owner, or a person responsible for the management of business, or a person who acts on behalf of a business owner with respect to matters relating to employees;3. The term "work" means both mental work and physical work.4. The term "labor contract" means a contract which is entered into in order that an employee offers work for which the employer pays its corresponding wages;5. The term "wages" means wages, salary and any other kinds of money or valuables, regardless of their titles, which the employer pays to an employee as remuneration for work;6. The term "average wages" means the amount calculated by dividing the total amount of wages paid to a relevant employee during three calendar months immediately before the day grounds for calculating his or her average wages occurred by the total number of calendar days during the three months. This shall apply mutatis mutandis to the employment of less than three months;7. The term "one week" means seven days including holidays;8. The term "contractual work hours" means work hours on which employees and their employer have made an agreement within the limit of work hours under Article 50 or the main clause of Article 69 of this Act, or under Article 139 (1) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act;9. The term "part-time employee" means an employee whose contractual work hours per week are shorter than those of a full-time employee engaged in the same kind of work at the workplace concerned.

path.text: Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Apr. 13, 2021; Jan. 11, 2022>1. The term "employee" means an employee as defined in Article 2 (1) 1 of the Labor Standards Act;2. The term "employer" means an employer as defined in Article 2 (1) 2 of the Labor Standards Act;3. The term "wages" means wages as defined in Article 2 (1) 5 of the Labor Standards Act;4. The term "average wages" means average wages as defined in Article 2 (1) 6 of the Labor Standards Act;5. The term "benefits" means an annuity or lump sum paid to employees under a retirement benefit scheme or an individual retirement pension scheme prescribed in Article 25;6. The term "retirement benefit scheme" means a defined benefit plan, a defined contribution plan, a SME retirement pension fund plan, and a retirement allowance system under Article 8;7. The term "retirement pension plan" means a defined benefit plan, a defined contribution plan, and an individual retirement pension plan;8. The term "defined benefit plan" means a retirement pension plan in which the amount of the benefits an employee will receive is predetermined;9. The term "defined contribution plan" means a retirement pension plan in which the amount of an employer's contribution to pay benefits is predetermined;10. The term "individual retirement pension plan" means a retirement pension plan established to accumulate and operate the lump sum paid by a participant or the contributions paid by an employer or a participant according to the participant's choice in which the amount of the benefits or contributions is not predetermined;11. The term "participant" means an employee who has joined a retirement pension plan or a SME retirement pension fund plan;12. The term "reserve" means money accumulated with contributions paid by an employer or a participant in order to pay benefits when a ground for the payment occurs, such as retirement of the participant;13. The term "retirement pension trustee" means a person registered in accordance with Article 26 in order to operate and manage the retirement pension plan or to manage its assets.14. The term "SME retirement pension fund plan" means a scheme of providing benefits to employees by creating and operating a mutual fund with contributions, etc. paid by at least two employers and employees of a small and medium enterprise to support a stable livelihood of the employees in their old age (limited to business employing not more than 30 regular employees; hereinafter the same shall apply);15. The term "default option scheme" means a scheme of operating a reserve by a method designated in advance if the participants fail to voluntarily select the operation method of the reserve;16. The term "default option management plan" means an operation method approved under Article 21-2 (1) to operate the reserve in accordance with a default option scheme.

q: If Person A's computer input had resulted in the actual transfer of funds and acquisition of benefits, what punishment could they face? Is it possible to punish Person A even if they did not actually acquire any benefits? When does the statute of limitations begin in this case?
a: If Person A entered false information into the company's computer system and actually acquired financial benefits, they could be subject to imprisonment for up to 10 years or a fine of up to 20 million won under Article 347-2 of the Criminal Act. Even if no actual benefit was obtained, an attempt to commit the crime can still be punished. The statute of limitations for such a crime begins from the time the criminal act is completed, which in this case would be from the point when the attempt to transfer funds ceased and the criminal act was effectively terminated.

q: In the event that the security deposit is not returned despite the termination of the lease agreement, how is the lease relationship evaluated? What is the legal nature of the profits obtained by Person A through the new lease, and what procedures must Person B follow to exercise the right to terminate or rescind the contract?
a: According to Article 9, Paragraph 2 of the Commercial Building Lease Protection Act, even if the lease has ended, the lease relationship is considered to continue if the tenant has not received the return of the security deposit. Furthermore, if Person A has obtained profits by re-leasing the premises to a third party while the lease with Person B has not been substantively terminated, this may be considered unjust enrichment under Article 741 of the Civil Code, as Person A has gained benefits by using another's property without legal cause, and thus may be subject to restitution. Meanwhile, for Person B to assert the right to terminate or rescind the contract, they must express this intention to Person A, the counterparty, in accordance with Article 543, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Code, for it to take effect.

q: What documents must Gapsan Forest Stone Company submit annually to the Director of the Korea Forest Service, Person B? What actions can the Director, Person B, undertake in relation to forest land conversion or stone extraction? Lastly, what procedures must Person B follow to designate or re-designate a quarry site?
a:
Gapsan Forest Stone Company is required to submit the previous year's business performance report and financial statement, as well as the current year's business plan and budget statement, to the Director of the Korea Forest Service, Person B, by the end of February each year. 

The Director, Person B, may demand reports, request the submission of materials, and enter the forest land for inspection from those engaged in forest land conversion or stone extraction. 

Furthermore, if Person B intends to designate or re-designate a quarry site, they must review whether the site meets the detailed designation criteria set forth in Article 6 of the Enforcement Decree of the Forest Land Management Act and assess the economic feasibility of the quarry as per Article 26(1) of the same decree. This process requires prior consultation with the heads of relevant administrative agencies and must undergo deliberation by the Central Forest Land Management Committee or the Local Forest Land Management Committee.

q: In the case where Person A and Person B conspired to make a false report, resulting in the entry of incorrect information in the original public deed, and used that document in an actual transaction, what crime under criminal law would they be punished for, and how does the fact that the crime was committed jointly affect the punishment?
a: Person A and Person B, by making a false report to a public official, caused incorrect information to be recorded in the original public deed, and thus, they are subject to punishment under Article 228, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Act, which prescribes imprisonment for up to five years or a fine of up to 10 million won. Additionally, since they used this document in an actual real estate transaction, they are also punishable under Article 229 of the Criminal Act with the same penalty. When such an offense is committed jointly by Person A and Person B, each is punished as a principal offender under Article 30 of the Criminal Act. Therefore, both Person A and Person B are individually subject to punishment as principal offenders for the crime of falsifying and using the original public deed.

q: In the case where Person B entered into a high-value contract without authority and signed a promissory note exceeding their authority as an agent for Person A, and the note was subsequently altered, what legal liabilities do Person A or Person B incur for each act?
a: If Person C had reasonable grounds to believe that Person B had the authority to enter into the contract, Person A is liable for the contract under Article 126 of the Civil Act. Regarding the promissory note, since Person B signed it in a state of unauthorized agency or exceeding authority, Person B bears direct obligations under the note pursuant to Article 8 of the Bills of Exchange and Promissory Notes Act. If the wording of the note was altered and Person B signed after the alteration, Person B is liable based on the altered wording according to Article 69 of the Bills of Exchange and Promissory Notes Act.

q: When Person B, who has become subject to personal information registration due to a sexual violence crime, intends to stay abroad for more than six months, what personal information must be reported in advance to the local police station, and what penalties may be imposed for failing to comply without a legitimate reason?
a: If Person B intends to stay abroad for more than six months, they must report in advance to the head of the local police station the country of stay and the duration of stay. At this time, Person B must accurately submit basic personal information, including their name, resident registration number, address and actual residence, occupation and workplace location, contact information, physical information (height, weight), and the registration number of any owned vehicles. If Person B fails to report this information without a legitimate reason or reports false information, they may be subject to imprisonment for up to one year or a fine of up to 5 million Korean Won.

q: In the case where Person A maliciously uses and profits from Person B's real estate without authorization, how is the scope of restitution and the interest rate determined?
a: As an obligor of unjust enrichment, Person A is required to return the unjustly obtained benefits to Person B pursuant to Article 741 of the Civil Code. If Person A is a malicious beneficiary, they must also pay interest on the benefits at the statutory rate of 5% per annum, as stipulated in Article 379 of the Civil Code, from the time of malicious intent, in accordance with Article 748(2) of the Civil Code. Additionally, if Person B has suffered damages, Person A must compensate for those damages.

q: On what basis should Person A establish the severance pay system for Person B Corporation, and how is average wage defined?
a: Person A should establish a system where severance pay is at least equivalent to 30 days' worth of average wages for each year of continuous service. The average wage is defined as the total amount of wages paid to the employee during the three months preceding the date on which the reason for calculating the average wage occurred, divided by the total number of days in that period.

path.text: The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on Mar. 20, 2018; Jan. 15, 2019; May 26, 2020>1. The term "employee" means a person, regardless of the kind of occupation, who offers labor to business or a workplace for the purpose of earning wages;2. The term "employer" means a business owner, or a person responsible for the management of business, or a person who acts on behalf of a business owner with respect to matters relating to employees;3. The term "work" means both mental work and physical work.4. The term "labor contract" means a contract which is entered into in order that an employee offers work for which the employer pays its corresponding wages;5. The term "wages" means wages, salary and any other kinds of money or valuables, regardless of their titles, which the employer pays to an employee as remuneration for work;6. The term "average wages" means the amount calculated by dividing the total amount of wages paid to a relevant employee during three calendar months immediately before the day grounds for calculating his or her average wages occurred by the total number of calendar days during the three months. This shall apply mutatis mutandis to the employment of less than three months;7. The term "one week" means seven days including holidays;8. The term "contractual work hours" means work hours on which employees and their employer have made an agreement within the limit of work hours under Article 50 or the main clause of Article 69 of this Act, or under Article 139 (1) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act;9. The term "part-time employee" means an employee whose contractual work hours per week are shorter than those of a full-time employee engaged in the same kind of work at the workplace concerned.

q: In the event that an air pollution alert is issued in Songpa-gu, what measures should the car repair shop operated by Person A take, and what are the pollutants targeted by the air pollution alerts?
a: The measures that Person A's car repair shop should take in response to the stages of air pollution alerts in Songpa-gu are as follows: If an advisory is issued, residents may be requested to refrain from outdoor activities and limit the use of automobiles. If a warning is issued, there may be requests to restrict outdoor activities, limit automobile use, and recommendations to reduce fuel consumption at business establishments. In the event of a severe alert, there may be requests to prohibit outdoor activities, bans on automobile traffic, and orders to reduce operating hours at business establishments. The pollutants targeted by the air pollution alerts are particulate matter (PM-10), fine particulate matter (PM-2.5), and ozone (O3).

q: When Person B establishes or amends a river construction implementation plan, what specific details must be included in the plan, and which of these details must be announced in the official gazette or public bulletin?
a: The river construction implementation plan must include the name, purpose, and summary of the river construction; the location of the implementation area; the name and address of the implementer; the expected start and completion dates; the specifications of the objects or rights to be acquired or used, along with the names and addresses of the owners or rights holders; the detailed design documents; the project budget and funding plan; the construction schedule; matters related to the management of river facilities; and the anticipated area of land to be generated from riverbed changes. Among these, the name, purpose, and summary of the river construction; the location of the implementation area; the name and address of the implementer; the expected start and completion dates; and the specifications of the objects or rights to be acquired or used, along with the names and addresses of the owners or rights holders, must be announced in the official gazette or public bulletin.

q: What procedural notification must Person A provide to Person B, the head of the relevant local government, when establishing a new zoning district in a part of City A and announcing it on the topographic map? What are the requirements for the new zoning district to be validly established, and how should this information be made available to the public?
a: Before Person A can designate a new zoning district and announce it on the topographic map, they must, in accordance with Article 8, Paragraph 8 of the Framework Act on the Regulation of Land Use, notify Person B, the head of the relevant local government, in advance of the related documents and the scheduled date of announcement, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. Additionally, the new zoning district that Person A intends to establish must conform to one of the following criteria under Article 5 of the same Act: (1) a district stipulated in the annex, (2) a district prescribed by Presidential Decree pursuant to delegation by other laws, or (3) a district announced in the official gazette by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport pursuant to delegation by Prime Ministerial Decree, Ministerial Decree, or local government regulations. The establishment of a zoning district that does not meet these requirements is not legally permissible. Finally, to provide the public with information on the designation of such zoning districts and related activity restrictions, information must be disclosed on a parcel-by-parcel basis through the Land Use Information System, as stipulated in Article 9, Paragraph 1 of the same Act.

q: In the situation where Person B has clearly expressed their intention not to perform the contract, what legal effect arises when Person A prepares and completes their performance and notifies Person B of this completion, demanding acceptance?
a: When Person B explicitly indicates their intention not to fulfill their contractual obligations, under Article 544 of the Civil Code, Person A may terminate the contract without the need for a demand for performance. Furthermore, if Person A prepares the performance in accordance with the contract, notifies Person B of its completion, and demands acceptance, it is considered an offer of performance equivalent to actual performance under Articles 460 and 461 of the Civil Code, thereby releasing Person A from liability for non-performance from that point forward.

q: As Person A is filing an administrative lawsuit against the cancellation of the business permit by Person B, they wish to understand the purpose of the Administrative Litigation Act and how multiple related appeals can be processed under the Administrative Appeals Act.
a: The purpose of the Administrative Litigation Act is to provide relief for the infringement of citizens' rights or interests caused by unlawful dispositions or other exercises or non-exercises of public authority by administrative agencies, and to appropriately resolve disputes concerning public law rights or the application of law. Additionally, under the Administrative Appeals Act, the commission may, if necessary, consolidate related appeals for joint examination or separate consolidated related appeals for individual examination.

The term "assistant architect" means any of the following persons who has filed a report with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, from among persons who belong to architectural firms under Article 23 and assist with services under Article 19:(a) A person who is undergoing or has undergone practical training under Article 13;(b) A person who has obtained a qualification of an engineer or industrial engineer in the fields of construction, electricity and electronics, machinery, chemistry, material, information and communications, environment and energy, or safety control pursuant to the National Technical Qualifications Act, or other fields prescribed by Presidential Decree;(c) A person who graduated from a university or college offering a four-year or longer architecture related degree course or who has a qualification equivalent thereto, and who has educational background and career experience prescribed by Presidential Decree;3. The term "design" means the following activities conducted by a certified architect, under his or her responsibility (including where an assistant's aid is received), for construction or major repair of buildings, alteration of the purpose of use, remodeling, installation of building equipment, or fabrication of structures:(a) Inspecting buildings, building equipment, structures, spatial environment, and planning of construction, etc.;(b) Preparing drawings, structural plans, construction design description and other necessary documents for construction prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (hereinafter referred to as "design documents");(c) Interpreting and advising the intent of the design documents;4. The term "construction supervision" means activities that a certified architect conducts under his or her responsibility (including cases where an assistant's aid is received) to confirm whether a building, building equipment, or structures have been constructed according to the details of the design documents, and to provide guidance on or superintend quality control, construction control, safety control, etc. in accordance with the Building Act;5. The term "practice of architecture" means carrying on business consisting of the provision of services referred to in Article 19, for a certain amount of compensation at another person's request.[This Article Wholly Amended on May 30, 2011]

q: What procedures must Person A follow to make a phone call to Person B, and how can the content of the call be managed?
a: Person A may make a phone call to Person B, who is outside the correctional facility, with the warden's permission. This permission may be granted on the condition that the content of the call is subject to monitoring or recording.

q: What documents must Person A submit to receive the interest expense deduction for a reverse mortgage, and how can Person A verify if their apartment meets the housing requirements for the deduction?
a: Person A must submit a tax base final return form along with a certificate of interest expense for a reverse mortgage to the head of the tax office having jurisdiction over their tax residence. The housing requirements for the deduction stipulate that the property must either have a reverse mortgage guarantee under Article 2, Subparagraph 8-2 of the Korea Housing Finance Corporation Act or be a reverse mortgage from a financial institution. Additionally, the standard market value of the house subject to the mortgage must not exceed 1.2 billion won.

q: What are the reporting requirements for Person A before and after departing to stay abroad for more than six months?
a: Person A must submit a departure report, as prescribed by the Ministry of Justice, to the head of the competent police station before leaving the country. If, after submitting the departure application, Person A does not depart or cannot return by the scheduled date due to changes in circumstances, they must promptly inform the head of the competent police station.

q: When Person A, a victim of rental fraud, acquires and holds the property, how are the acquisition tax and property tax respectively reduced? Furthermore, what benefits apply to the registration license tax when Person A applies for a tenant's right registration order and registers the tenant's right?
a:
When Person A, a victim of rental fraud, acquires the property involved in the fraud, the acquisition tax calculated is fully exempted if it is 2 million Korean Won or less, and if it exceeds 2 million Korean Won, an amount of 2 million Korean Won is deducted, provided this occurs by December 31, 2026.

Since the property has a dedicated area of 60 square meters or less, Person A will receive a 50% reduction in property tax for three years from the date the obligation to pay property tax first arises.

Additionally, for the tenant's right registration made pursuant to the tenant's right registration order applied for by Person A to protect their rights, the registration license tax is exempted until December 31, 2026.

q: In the case where the CEO of the publicly listed XYZ Corporation, Person A, provides credit to a major shareholder, Person B, without board approval, what legal liabilities does Person A incur? Is there a possibility of criminal liability for XYZ Corporation itself?
a: Person A, the CEO, violated Article 542-9, Paragraph 1 of the Korean Commercial Act by providing credit to a major shareholder without board approval. This violation subjects Person A to potential penalties under Article 624-2 of the same Act, which include imprisonment for up to five years or a fine of up to 200 million KRW. Furthermore, if it is proven that Person A's violation is related to the company's business, XYZ Corporation may also be subject to a fine under the dual liability provision of Article 634-3 of the Korean Commercial Act.

path.text: Article 634-3 (Joint Penalty Provisions) If the representative of a company, or an agent or employee of, or any other person employed, by a company commits a violation under Article 624-2 in connection with the business affairs of the company, not only shall such violator be punished, but also the company shall be punished by a fine under the relevant provisions: Provided, That this shall not apply where such company has not been negligent in giving due attention and supervision concerning the relevant duties to prevent such violation, including where it has faithfully performed its duty under Article 542-13. <Amended by Act No. 10600, Apr. 14, 2011>[This Article Newly Inserted by Act No. 9362, Jan. 30, 2009]

q: In a situation where a single act constitutes both theft and fraud, with a final verdict already rendered for the theft charge and the fraud charge still under trial, what legal effect does a pardon for the fraud charge have on Person A, and what is the overall punishment?
a:
Person A's act constitutes an ideal concurrence of offenses under Article 40 of the Criminal Code, where a single act constitutes multiple crimes.

Since a final guilty verdict has already been rendered for the theft charge, the court must render a judgment of dismissal for the fraud charge pursuant to Article 326(1) of the Criminal Procedure Act.

Although a special pardon has been granted for the fraud charge, Article 326(2) of the Criminal Procedure Act applies to general pardons and is therefore not applicable in this case.

path.text: Article 40 (Compound Crimes) When a single act constitutes several crimes, the punishment provided for the most severe crime shall be imposed.[This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 8, 2020]
